title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Golden Cross Signals 34% Average Rally for BTC
summary: Bitcoin nears a rare golden cross linked to 34% average gains as improving on-chain signals and US midterms raise hopes of an October bottom.
content:
Bitcoin ( BTC ) is approaching a rare golden cross on its three-day chart, a bullish technical signal associated with an average 33.78% price rally across three historical examples.

The crossover could form as early as this week, potentially strengthening Bitcoin's broader recovery outlook as improving macroeconomic and on-chain conditions raise hopes of an October bottom.

Bitcoin's three-day chart shows its 20-period exponential moving average (20-3D EMA) approaching a crossover above the 200-period EMA (200-3D EMA) .

The formation, commonly known as a golden cross, occurs when a shorter-term moving average rises above a longer-term one, signaling improving momentum and potentially the beginning of a sustained bullish trend.

Historical examples highlighted on the chart suggest the setup has preceded substantial BTC price advances.

In 2019, Bitcoin rallied approximately 50.73% following a similar bullish moving-average configuration. The 2020 occurrence was associated with an 18.38% advance, while another instance in 2023–2024 saw BTC climb roughly 32.23%.

These three rallies produced an average gain of 33.78% , underscoring the pattern's historical bullish implications.

However, the gains unfolded over different timeframes, meaning the average should not be interpreted as a 30-day return or a guaranteed price target.

The latest formation comes as Bitcoin trades near $83,500, following its recovery from September's consolidation phase.

A confirmed golden cross could strengthen the bullish outlook, particularly if BTC continues establishing higher highs and higher lows.

Still, golden crosses are lagging indicators. Bitcoin could experience short-term pullbacks even after confirmation, while a sustained decline below the longer-term moving average would weaken the bullish thesis.

Bitcoin's potential golden cross coincides with signs that its October correction may be approaching exhaustion, according to an analysis by xWIN.

Elevated US Treasury yields, high oil prices, slowing spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, and profit-taking have weighed on BTC, leaving leveraged positions vulnerable to liquidations.

However, some macroeconomic pressures appear to be easing.

As of Oct. 12, markets were pricing in roughly an 18% probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October , while Brent crude had retreated from nearly $110 to around $103 per barrel.

The Nov. 3 US midterm elections could provide another catalyst. Greater political clarity after the vote may encourage investors to reassess risk exposure, although uncertainty surrounding the closely contested Senate remains.

On-chain indicators also suggest improving conditions.

According to xWIN , Bitcoin exchange reserves remain relatively low despite a recent rebound, indicating that selling pressure from readily available exchange supply remains contained.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin's Apparent Demand has recovered sharply from deeply negative territory, although the metric has yet to turn positive.

Whale holdings have also increased to approximately 3 million BTC , remaining elevated throughout the recent price correction. This suggests large holders have continued accumulating or retaining exposure despite market weakness.

Together, these developments strengthen the case for a potential October bottom, complementing Bitcoin's emerging golden cross.

title: Bitmine Adds $32M in Ethereum as Tom Lee Says Firm Is Nearly 'Done Stacking'
summary: The Ethereum treasury firm now holds 6.03 million ETH, 4.9% of supply, as Lee predicts the biggest crypto bull market yet.
content:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies bought 12,532 ETH over the past week, worth about $31.9 million at the $2,544 price the company used to value its holdings and lifting its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, the company said Monday.

The stash represents 4.9% of the total 122.1 million Ethereum token supply, leaving the firm 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5%, a target it calls the "Alchemy of 5%."

Bitmine bought $41 million more ETH the week before. In a press release, the firm's Chairman Tom Lee claimed that its "track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world."

The company valued its ETH at $2,544 per token, and put its total crypto, cash and investment holdings at $16.2 billion. That includes 214 BTC, $612 million in cash and marketable securities, and stakes worth $180 million in Beast Industries and $85 million in Eightco Holdings.

The firm has staked 5,067,309 ETH, which Lee said generates annualized staking revenue of about $336 million.

In his monthly Chairman's message last week, Lee said Bitmine needs "about 100,000 more ETH, and that's about it." He has said the firm's Ethereum buying will stop once it reaches its target.

"Now we're done stacking while a bull market is starting," Lee said in the video. "So if we're done stacking, but ETH goes up a lot, you can imagine that we'll outperform Ethereum."

Lee predicted the crypto bull market would be "the biggest bull market we've ever seen," driven by tokenization, a wealth transfer to younger investors, supply absorbed by digital asset treasury firms, and AI agents using crypto wallets .

He said Bitmine shares, then around $26, are 90% correlated with ETH, and projected that ETH at $22,000 would put the stock at $300 to $500.

Lee also pointed to Bitmine's 9.5% perpetual preferred stock, BMNP, which was issued at $80 in June and last closed at $99.53, according to the release.

summary: Michael Saylor insists there is always room for more Bitcoin, but Strategy's latest weekly purchase raises a question worth asking: what does a near-microscopic acquisition reveal about the limits of the company's grand accumulation playbook?
content:
Strategy purchased just 334 Bitcoin for $28.7M last week, a dramatic drop from the 55,500 coins it bought in a single November 2024 week.

Saylor's buying pace tracks his stock's premium, since issuing shares below that premium would dilute shareholders' Bitcoin-per-share ratio.

The modest purchase keeps Strategy's accumulation model visible to shareholders but is too small to move Bitcoin's market price.

Between September 28 and October 4, 2026, Strategy Inc. ( NASDAQ:MSTR ) purchased 334 Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) for $28.7 million. This comes as executive chairman Michael Saylor notes that there is "always room for more orange," referring to Bitcoin's orange logo. However, this latest purchase suggests that the company has only made a small dent in that room.

Just two years prior, in November 2024, the company made headlines by buying approximately 55,500 Bitcoin in a single week. Currently, Strategy holds around 848,000 Bitcoin, making it the largest corporate holder of the digital currency.

As of October 12, Bitcoin is trading at about $83,400, down about 34% from its peak of $126,080. While the price is up 8% over the past 30 days, it has dipped 3% in the last week, suggesting the recent purchase of 334 coins is unlikely to affect the overall market. So, what does this smaller purchase indicate about a company whose main strategy is to accumulate more Bitcoin?

Originally named MicroStrategy, the company started as a business intelligence software provider. Although it still sells analytics software to corporate clients—increasingly through cloud subscriptions—most investors now focus on its Bitcoin holdings.

------

Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.

That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›

------

The company's Bitcoin strategy follows a two-step model. First, Strategy raises capital from investors by issuing new shares and other securities. Then, it uses that cash to buy Bitcoin. This allows investors to gain exposure to Bitcoin without needing to purchase or store it themselves.

The company's model works best when its stock trades at a premium, meaning investors pay more for each share than the Bitcoin it represents. In such cases, the money raised from selling new shares allows Strategy to buy more Bitcoin than what each share stands for, which benefits existing shareholders by increasing their Bitcoin per share. The large purchase of 55,500 coins in November 2024 occurred during a favorable financing period.

In contrast, acquiring 334 Bitcoin only adds about 0.04% to a total holding of 848,000 coins. This minimal increase hardly affects the overall amount of Bitcoin represented by each share.

The likely reason for this slowdown is the company's financing conditions. Strategy can easily raise funds for Bitcoin purchases when its shares carry a premium, but struggles when they don't. If that premium shrinks, selling more stock to buy Bitcoin dilutes each shareholder's stake in the Bitcoin the company holds.

Therefore, the pace of buying reflects market conditions rather than the company's commitment to Bitcoin.

Management has previously stated similar sentiments. During the February 5, 2026, earnings call, Saylor remarked, "When our equity trades weak, we don't sell it." Management further noted, "We wouldn't electively or programmatically issue equity to buy Bitcoin if it was going to decrease Bitcoin per share."

Saylor's statement about "always room for more orange" deserves scrutiny, as he leads a company whose stock is heavily influenced by Bitcoin sentiment. His comments don't specify the size, timeline, or funding source for future purchases. The weekly disclosure simply states what Strategy bought and how much it paid, without clarifying why the purchase was so small or promising a change in purchasing pace.

That said, the purchase, however modest, indicates the company is still active in the Bitcoin market. Holding onto approximately 848,000 coins suggests a commitment to building its Bitcoin treasury, even if the recent acquisition is small.

It's unclear why purchases have slowed. Strategy could be biding its time for more favorable financing conditions, or it could be facing limits on how much capital investors are willing to provide at the current price. The company has not disclosed which scenario is true.

Overall, Strategy stands to gain more than Bitcoin itself from these small purchases. Each acquisition, however minor, reassures shareholders that the model is still operational, keeping the stock relevant as a proxy for Bitcoin investment. On the other hand, the $28.7 million spent to buy 334 Bitcoin is too small to noticeably affect the market, with Bitcoin priced around $83,400. The company's own modest expenditure represents the only fresh demand it adds to the market.

The next 8-K filing—used by public companies to report significant events to the Securities and Exchange Commission—is expected after the October 12 federal holiday. A purchase of thousands of Bitcoin could signal improved financing conditions, suggesting the 334-coin purchase was merely a pause. Conversely, another purchase of just a few hundred coins, or none at all, would indicate that Strategy's buying activity remains constrained.

title: Jeonbuk’s BTC USD Loan Terms Remain Unclear as Banks Test Collateral
summary: Jeonbuk Bank has reportedly started offering Korean-won loans to corporate customers who pledge BTC USD for business operating funds, a reported first for a South Korean bank. Edaily reported the launch on October 12, 2026; Bitcoin is currently the only eligible digital asset, and the bank has not disclosed the ...
content:
Jeonbuk Bank has reportedly started offering Korean-won loans to corporate customers who pledge BTC USD for business operating funds, a reported first for a South Korean bank.

Edaily reported the launch on October 12, 2026; Bitcoin is currently the only eligible digital asset, and the bank has not disclosed the interest rate, loan-to-value ratio, or lending volume.

The limited launch is an institutional Bitcoin adoption signal: a regulated lender is applying familiar credit and collateral processes to Bitcoin without taking direct custody of the asset. The terms that would show how much financing companies can actually obtain remain unknown.

Corporate borrowers pledge BTC USD held by a specialist custodian registered under South Korean financial transaction reporting rules. Jeonbuk Bank provides the loan in won but does not directly own or control the pledged coins; proceeds are restricted to business operations.

The report does not identify the custodian or specify loan limits, maturities, collateral haircuts, margin-call thresholds, or liquidation triggers. Without those details, borrowers and market observers cannot assess how much a Bitcoin price drop could reduce available credit or prompt additional collateral requirements.

Custody is central to the structure: the bank lends against Bitcoin without operating the wallet that holds it. The Bitcoin custody model helps explain why signing controls and asset segregation matter when a lender relies on a third party to safeguard collateral.

Jeonbuk Bank has developed a valuation system that combines a weighted index from various global exchanges with a measure of market volatility to reduce reliance on any single exchange.

The bank chose Bitcoin for its market size, liquidity, and trading volume, and it conducts stress tests to assess its risk as collateral. These tests do not eliminate the risk that a rapid sell-off could reduce the collateral's value.

Eligible custodians must comply with security certifications and the Travel Rule, which requires sharing sender and recipient information for certain transfers. Under South Korea's Virtual Asset User Protection Act, custodians must also segregate customer assets and meet cold-storage requirements.

Revised civil-enforcement rules effective October 1, 2026, allow the bank to seek court approval to sell Bitcoin collateral if a borrower defaults, providing a potential recovery method, although the report doesn't specify the timeline for sales in volatile markets.

Jeonbuk Bank is a subsidiary of JB Financial Group. The report says it provides real-name deposit and withdrawal accounts to cryptocurrency exchanges, and describes it as the only regional bank in South Korea offering that arrangement.

The bank also has a team examining payment, remittance and stablecoin services, has conducted proof-of-concept work and is working with outside technology firms on an integrated wallet.

It plans to review other eligible assets and lending services as regulation, customer demand and operating experience develop. That broader infrastructure push reflects the banking sector's focus on digital assets discussed during South Korea's institutional crypto discussions .

The report places Jeonbuk's move alongside digital-asset financing initiatives from JPMorgan Chase, Sygnum and BitGo, without establishing that their products use identical terms.

For now, the defining feature of Jeonbuk's Bitcoin-backed loans is their narrow scope: corporate use, Bitcoin collateral, third-party custody and recovery through a court-supervised sale. Whether the product expands will depend on the bank's experience and the direction of South Korea's crypto regulation.

title: Strategy Scoops Up $21.5M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $192M in STRC
summary: The purchase lifts Strategy's holdings to 848,250 BTC and follows a $176 million repurchase of STRC preferred stock the week before.
content:
Strategy bought 250 BTC last week and spent $192.4 million repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, the company said on Monday.

The Bitcoin treasury firm paid $21.5 million for the coins between October 5 and October 11, an average of $86,194 per Bitcoin including fees, according to its release. It now holds 848,250 BTC, a new record, acquired for a total of $64 billion at an average of $75,444 per coin.

Strategy raised $21 million by selling about 125,000 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, and used $500,000 of cash to cover the rest. It sold none of its preferred stock during the week.

The company repurchased 1,932,145 shares of STRC, its variable-rate Stretch preferred stock, leaving $354.8 million available under its program to buy back preferred shares.

Last week, Strategy bought $29 million in Bitcoin and repurchased $176 million of STRC as it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.

As of October 11, Strategy held $4.88 billion in a U.S. dollar reserve set aside for preferred dividends and debt interest, and $640.5 million in cash for broader purposes such as buying Bitcoin.

Strategy set up its USD reserve with $1.44 billion, and later established the separate USD cash pot after raising $2 billion by selling MSTR stock.

The company has also proposed that its preferred stock dividends accrue 365 days a year, and has said it could sell up to $1.25 billion of Bitcoin under its digital credit capital framework.

Strategy CEO Phong Le defended selling Bitcoin as the "right trade" in September, weeks before the firm set a new holdings record at the end of the month with a $143 million purchase. Despite the uptick in buying, traders on prediction market Myriad, owned by Decrypt 's parent company Dastan, do not expect the firm's holdings to surpass one million BTC by the end of the year, putting just a 5% chance on that outcome.

title: Bitcoin’s Next Move Depends on the US Bond Market and Inflation Report
summary: Bitcoin faces further selling pressure as US Treasury yields surge to a 24-year high. Bitunix explains the risks ahead of key US inflation data.
content:
Bitcoin's next major move could depend on the US bond market. Treasury yields surged to their highest level in 24 years, making government bonds more attractive to investors and putting fresh pressure on cryptocurrencies.

According to Bitunix's October market analysis, the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed above 5.35%. Bitcoin fell below $82,000, while selling spread across the wider crypto market.

The exchange warns that continued pressure from high bond yields could make a sustained crypto recovery difficult.

US Treasury bonds offer investors regular interest payments backed by the government. When their yields rise, investors can earn higher returns without taking the same risks associated with cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin pays no fixed interest. As a result, higher Treasury yields can encourage investors to move capital into government bonds or hold cash.

Bitunix argues that this shift in investor preferences is creating additional pressure on Bitcoin and other speculative assets.

The risk extends beyond crypto. Higher yields also increase borrowing costs and can reduce the appeal of technology stocks. Bitunix reported weekly declines in crypto-linked equities, including Strategy and Circle.

However, the direction of bond yields remains critical. A sustained decline could improve investor appetite for risk and help Bitcoin recover.

The broader crypto market suffered even heavier losses during October 3–9.

Bitcoin declined 3.80%, while Ethereum lost 8.39% and XRP fell 7.09%.

More importantly, only around 20% of the top 300 cryptocurrencies tracked by Bitunix recorded gains. Their median weekly return was -5.18%.

Decentralized finance tokens also struggled. Uniswap's UNI declined 18.37%, while PancakeSwap's CAKE lost 15.92%.

Yet speculative trading continues.

The Sandbox's SAND rallied 57.71%, even as Bitunix found little evidence of improving project fundamentals. The exchange attributed the move primarily to trading sentiment and capital flows, although it could not establish the precise drivers.

Meanwhile, commodities followed a different path. Gold returned to $4,200, while Brent crude climbed above $100 per barrel.

The next major test comes on October 14, when the US releases September's Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Bitunix cites an expected annual inflation rate of 3.6%, up from the previous 3.4%.

Higher-than-expected inflation could strengthen expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates elevated. Treasury yields could rise further, creating additional selling pressure on Bitcoin and other risk assets.

Conversely, softer inflation could ease pressure on bond yields and support a crypto recovery.

For traders, the key signal will be how Treasury yields react to the CPI data.

Bitunix's central warning is that Bitcoin could remain vulnerable to further losses while US government bonds continue offering unusually attractive returns.

title: South Korea’s Jeonbuk Bank Lends Won Against Bitcoin, Using Court Sales for Defaults
summary: The South Korean lender confirmed a corporate loan secured by custodied BTC but has not disclosed its size, interest rate or loan-to-value ratio.
content:
Jeonbuk Bank , a regional South Korean lender, has extended a corporate loan in won secured by Bitcoin , under a setup in which the bank never takes possession of the coins, even if the borrower defaults.

Local outlet Edaily first reported the loan on Oct. 12, describing it as the first of its kind from a South Korean bank. A Jeonbuk Bank spokesperson confirmed to Jaekyung Ilbo that a loan had actually been made but said the borrower could not be disclosed. The bank, a unit of JB Financial Group , has not published a press release or filing on the product, or the date the loan was made.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter .

For now, the product is open only to corporate customers, accepts only Bitcoin as collateral and limits the proceeds to business operating funds, according to the reports. The pledged BTC sits with a third-party custodian, and the bank has neither ownership of it nor direct control over it. The bank has restricted the custodian role to virtual asset service providers registered under Korea's financial reporting law.

If a borrower defaults, the bank would not receive the Bitcoin. It would instead convert the collateral to cash through court enforcement, such as a sale order, and repay itself from the proceeds. That route depends on the Supreme Court of Korea's amended Civil Enforcement Rules , which the outlets said took effect Oct. 1 and set procedures for seizing and liquidating virtual assets.

The bank values the collateral with its own multi-exchange price benchmark and stress-tested it against sharp Bitcoin price drops, according to Edaily.

The loan was designed to use the bank's existing lending and collateral systems "without directly holding virtual assets," Jeong Sang-hoon, executive vice president of the bank's digital division, said in Edaily's English-language edition.

The loan-to-value ratio , interest rate and loan size were not disclosed, TechM reported . A bank spokesperson told the outlet the loan fell within the lending business allowed under Korea's Banking Act and had not received a regulatory sandbox designation.

No Korean statute explicitly bars crypto as loan collateral, but a 2017 to 2018 government crackdown included a ban on financial firms lending against virtual assets, which hardened into a de facto rule, according to Jaekyung Ilbo. Edaily and Jaekyung Ilbo reported that the bank plans to weigh widening the eligible collateral and services later, based on regulatory changes and demand.

The loan is the first product of CEO Park Chun-won's "Crypto Bank" plan, according to Edaily. Park signaled crypto-collateral lending earlier this year.

Edaily cited JPMorgan Chase and Switzerland's Sygnum Bank as lenders already offering similar credit overseas. In June 2025, JPMorgan was reported to be planning to accept crypto ETFs as loan collateral , which involves fund shares rather than Bitcoin held directly.

content:
SWI Group has raised €800 million from institutional investors at a €6.1 billion valuation. The Singapore-incorporated, Amsterdam-listed company is repositioning former FTX backed Bitcoin miner Genesis Digital Assets around AI infrastructure and marketing its sites to hyperscale cloud providers .

SWI plans to market Genesis Digital facilities in Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Sweden to hyperscale cloud providers. The company says Genesis Digital has more than 1.3 gigawatts of energized and approved grid connections across 15 facilities. Combined with AiOnX, SWI's European platform, the group says it has more than 3.6GW.

SWI's move follows its June 15 purchase of about 38.3% of Genesis Digital's shares for $500 million. The deal also included 77.2% of the $1.124 billion liquidation preference on Genesis Digital's preferred stock; SWI has since moved to majority ownership.

The company is applying a familiar infrastructure thesis to a Bitcoin mining business: grid access may be more valuable than the economics of mining at a particular site. That thesis is increasingly relevant as operators seek to adapt energy-intensive facilities for AI and high-performance computing.

After FTX collapsed, estate administrators sued Genesis Digital to recover the investment, calling it one of Bankman-Fried's most reckless investments and describing its Kazakh assets as virtually worthless, according to the Wall Street Journal.

FTX dropped the lawsuit on June 15, the same day SWI closed its initial stake purchase. SWI founder and CEO Max-Hervé George said all legal disputes with FTX and other shareholders had been settled.

SWI's stated next steps are limited and concrete: market the four named locations to hyperscale cloud providers, sell the three small Kazakhstan mining sites, and deploy the new capital into infrastructure, compute, and its development pipeline across Europe and the US.

title: Arthur Hayes Thinks FLOP Could Outgrow Bitcoin. Its Testnet Is Weeks Away
summary: Arthur Hayes says the FLOP testnet ships within weeks. See how his Bitcoin-style AI mining network pays GPU owners and who earns the airdrop.
content:
Arthur Hayes says Flop Labs will ship the FLOP testnet within weeks. The 90-day trial is the only route to the project's genesis airdrop, so miners, validators, and AI agents must earn their share.

Yet Flop Labs' own testnet page sets no launch date. Instead, it ties the start to readiness criteria and allows an extension if the team misses them.

Hayes, the BitMEX co-founder who left retirement to lead Flop Labs in August, posted the update after TOKEN2049 Singapore.

The startup is building a blockchain where AI agents rent computing power. Agents would pay in FLOP whenever they need a model to answer a request or storage for their data.

The miners here are GPU owners. These are people or data centers with graphics processing units (GPUs), the chips that also run AI models like ChatGPT.

Bitcoin miners spend electricity guessing numbers to secure their network, and that work has no other use. By contrast, Flop's proof-of-useful-inference model pays miners for real AI tasks.

In return, miners earn block rewards plus most of the inference fees. Validators, meanwhile, confirm that the work actually happened. Hayes first sketched the idea in his creation-style FLOP pitch.

The testnet rehearses that market with worthless test tokens. Miners earn credit only for verified compute, so idle hardware scores nothing.

Validators compete for 1,000 mainnet seats based on their testnet ranking. Agents, in contrast, must actually spend faucet tokens on inference, because holding them earns nothing.

FLOP borrows heavily from Bitcoin's design. Blocks arrive about every second, and each one pays 96 FLOP to miners.

That reward halves every 730 days, echoing the Bitcoin halving cycle at twice the pace. A September draft caps supply near 18.1 billion tokens after 10 years, with 24.3% reserved for the airdrop.

The project also skips the usual fundraising. It has no presale and no venture capital allocation, and Hayes says he funded the team himself.

Hayes goes further. He cites Reed's Law, the idea that a network's value soars as users form groups, to argue Flop could one day be worth more than Bitcoin.

However, no published model backs that claim. The Yellow Paper is still a draft at version 0.5.0, and the team flags many of its figures as provisional.

The FLOP testnet also launches into a crowded field. Render and Ocean Network already rent out idle GPUs for AI work.

Hayes expects the AI data center boom to overbuild and end in a bailout. Meanwhile, the FLOP testnet will show whether his own AI venture can draw real demand for compute.

title: China Crypto Strategy Expands as Beijing Backs National Blockchain Network

content:
China announced crypto plans for a national blockchain network. The proposal appeared in a policy document from the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council, made public by Xinhua. The document frames blockchain within a wider digital-economy expansion, while mainland China's ban on cryptocurrency transactions remains in place.

The Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China

The China policy document, titled "Opinions of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council on Developing New Productive Forces," makes no mention of Bitcoin or other independent crypto. Its broader agenda includes digitizing manufacturing, building a national integrated computing-power network, and advancing the "Eastern Data, Western Computing" project, which shifts data storage and computing activity toward western regions.

Beijing's support for blockchain as infrastructure may create opportunities in enterprise and government systems, but it does not amount to permission for mainland residents to trade private cryptocurrencies. China's existing state-backed Blockchain-based Service Network (BSN) supports government and business applications while prohibiting cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin from operating on its rails.

Whether the proposed national system builds on BSN is possible but unconfirmed. The policy also cautions against prioritizing virtual activity over the real economy or creating bubbles, a signal that the stated objective is practical integration with manufacturing and other economic activity, not unrestricted token speculation.

Related blockchain applications include atomic settlement of tokenized assets and regulated controls for on-chain financial products , but neither establishes how China's network will be designed.

The China narrative can attract speculative demand quickly, while any durable fundamental case would require evidence of a role in pilots, standards, or deployed infrastructure. Solana's 62% drop from its $293 all-time high is three times Bitcoin's 20% loss from the same January 2025 entry date.

So, if Solana's technology delivered on its promises, why did its price fall so much more than Bitcoin's?

On October 9, Solana's network reduced its block time to just 200 milliseconds, making it the fastest among major blockchains. Block time is how quickly a blockchain records a new batch of transactions; shorter times mean faster confirmations for payments or trades. Solana's developers are also planning an upgrade called Alpenglow, which aims to improve final settlement speed further.

Businesses often choose a blockchain based on speed. For example, payment processing at a checkout, executing an order in a trading app, or tracking moves in a game all require rapid confirmations. title: Treasury Yields Are Now Above 5%. Here's Why That's Bearish For Bitcoin.
summary: Investors shouldn't conflate the devaluation of fiat currencies with rising Treasury yields.
content:
The 10-Year Treasury yield recently hit 5.3%, its highest level since 2007. As a result, issuers of CDs, bonds, and other fixed-income investments will need to raise their yields to stay competitive. That shift could draw investors away from stocks and other riskier investments.

Some investors might argue that Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) is immune to that shift because it's becoming a safe-haven hedge against the debasement of fiat currencies. But at $84,000, Bitcoin remains about 33% below its all-time high of $126,000 from last October. Let's see why higher yields are weighing down Bitcoin -- and why it might bounce back if those yields decline.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Bitcoin is mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work ( PoW ) consensus mechanism, which relies on powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles. But every four years, a scheduled "halving" halves those rewards, making it even harder to mine Bitcoin profitably.

More than 20 million of Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million tokens have already been mined, but its increasing difficulty will prevent its last token from being mined until 2140. That scarcity makes it more comparable to gold than many other cryptocurrencies, so it's often considered a hedge against inflation and the devaluation of the U.S. dollar.

However, rising Treasury yields also usually drive investors away from gold. While gold might be a good hedge against a weakening dollar, rising yields actually strengthen the U.S. dollar. As that happens, it makes more sense for investors to shift from gold toward low-risk CDs, Treasuries, bonds, and other fixed-income investments that pay guaranteed interest. At the same time, rising borrowing costs will prevent investors from taking on riskier, leveraged bets and drive them to liquidate more volatile investments to fund their fixed-income purchases.

Bitcoin, as "digital gold," is exposed to the same headwinds. Many institutional investors will also rotate out of Bitcoin ETFs -- which provide exposure to Bitcoin without crypto wallets and keys -- as Treasury yields rise. So while Bitcoin and gold still might be good long-term bets against the U.S. dollar and other fiat currencies, they won't bounce back unless the Treasury yields cool off and risk-seeking investors return to the market.

I'm still bullish on Bitcoin's long-term growth potential, since monetary expansion policies will inevitably debase fiat currencies. But investors shouldn't conflate that debasement with the near-term pressures of rising interest rates and Treasury yields. Those challenges could prevent Bitcoin from revisiting its all-time highs for the foreseeable future.

title: Bots are Changing South Korea’s Famous Bitcoin Price Gap
summary: South Korea’s Kimchi Premium is no longer a simple story of human traders chasing price gaps: all you need to know.
content:
Bitcoin can cost more in South Korea than it does almost anywhere else. For years, traders chased that gap for profit. Now, automated trading is making the race faster, while strict banking rules still decide who can take part.

The price difference, known as the Kimchi Premium, was once a popular sign of Korean investors rushing into crypto. Its meaning is becoming harder to read.

The trade sounds simple: buy Bitcoin cheaply abroad, transfer it to a Korean exchange, and sell it for more.

But South Korea restricts cross-border money transfers. Traders cannot always move their profits back overseas freely. That helps explain why the premium can survive even when everyone sees it.

Historically, a widening gap often signaled strong local demand. Investors watched it for clues that retail speculation was heating up.

Evidence suggests some traders have already automated the process.

A June 2026 study examined 16,228 arbitrage transactions between Binance and Bithumb. Researchers found 96% took place within five-minute intervals, pointing to possible automated trading.

That does not prove AI agents control the market. But it shows how difficult it can be for manual traders to compete with software.

Korea's tighter investor-protection rules add another obstacle. Exchanges face greater oversight, while restrictions on moving money across borders still limit who can exploit the spread.

The gap can widen when Korean buyers get aggressive. It can also reflect slower selling, currency changes, or shifts in local market sentiment.

Meanwhile, retail demand remains substantial. Chainalysis estimates South Korea's crypto economy at $449 billion over its latest study period, with investors particularly interested in AI-linked tokens.

Proposed won-backed stablecoins could eventually make settlement easier, if regulators permit them.

For investors, a rising Kimchi Premium still matters. But treating it as automatic proof of a buying frenzy risks missing what is happening behind the prices.

title: Bitcoin Could Be Entering a New Bull Market Despite Latest Sell-Off
summary: BloFin Research says Bitcoin's new bull market remains intact despite the latest sell-off, as historical data suggests its boom-and-bust cycles are weakening.
content:
Despite the market dip and liquidations over the past week, Bitcoin has seemingly entered a bull market, as the analysis of its 50-week moving average shows.

BloFin Research argues that Bitcoin's traditional four-year boom-and-bust cycle is gradually losing strength. Future rallies could deliver smaller gains, followed by shorter and less severe downturns.

The strongest evidence comes from Bitcoin's recovery above its 50-week moving average, a technical indicator that previously signaled bull-market transitions in 2015, 2019 and 2023.

Bitcoin reclaimed this level near $78,800 in September. It subsequently traded above $86,000 in early October.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin's MVRV ratio, which compares its current market value with the average price investors paid for their coins, moved above its annual average.

As of October 11, MVRV stood near 1.54, above its 365-day average of 1.44. This suggests the longer-term recovery remains intact despite recent selling.

It means Bitcoin's market strength is improving, a signal that has previously appeared during the early stages of bull markets.

BloFin's most significant finding concerns the declining severity of Bitcoin's market cycles.

Bitcoin fell approximately 53% from its October 2025 peak of $124,824 to $58,525 in June 2026.

Previous bear markets were considerably worse:

Bull-market gains have also narrowed. Bitcoin's trough-to-peak returns have declined from roughly 530 times in its earliest cycle to eight times in the most recent one.

If June remains the bottom, the latest bear market lasted approximately eight months, compared with 12–13 months historically.

BloFin Research attributes much of this change to longer-term ownership. In September, approximately 16.64 million BTC, or 83% of circulating supply, had remained unmoved for at least 155 days.

Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin ETFs held around 1.3 million BTC on October 2. Public companies owned another 1.29 million BTC.

Together, ETFs and corporate treasuries controlled approximately 13% of circulating Bitcoin.

However, last week's $679 million ETF outflow shows that institutional demand can still weaken sharply during market stress.

Bitcoin was trading around $83,000 on October 11, still above the September moving-average breakout level and well above its June low.

The four-year cycle also remains visible. Bitcoin peaked roughly 18 months after the April 2024 halving, consistent with historical patterns.

For traders, a sustained move below the current 50-week moving average would weaken the bullish signal. A break beneath $58,525 would challenge the proposed cycle bottom.

For now, Bitcoin's longer-term recovery indicators remain positive. The recent ETF withdrawals show why the transition toward a more stable market could still involve sharp corrections.

title: Oil Traders Are About to Test Trump’s Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Claim, But Bitcoin Reacted First
summary: Bitcoin rose on Trump’s Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire claim. Oil futures reopen next to test a truce neither side confirmed.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) rose to $84,000 on Sunday after President Donald Trump declared an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv confirmed the deal.

Oil futures have been closed since Friday. When they reopen Sunday evening in New York, energy traders get their first chance to price a truce that rests on a single post.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that both sides had agreed and warned them not to break it. He gave no terms, start time, or way to check compliance.

Crypto markets moved anyway. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum prices rose in the immediate aftermath of the news, albeit modest gains.

The rise hit traders betting on a fall. A liquidation happens when an exchange force-closes a borrowed bet that has lost too much.

CoinGlass data showed $70 million in short bets wiped out over four hours. Long liquidations totaled only $6.9 million.

Shorts made up 97.1% of the $22.29 million liquidated on Bitcoin in that window. The reaction contrasts with June, when BTC barely moved on the Senate's Iran vote.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the announcement was "news for me." He then set out his terms.

"If President Trump negotiated it with Putin, please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready, and we will accept it," Axios reported, citing Zelensky.

Still, it is important to note that the EU is preparing additional funding for Ukrainian drones and missiles, even as Zelensky mulls a possible ceasefire on energy infrastructure.

Moscow had not commented by press time. On October 8, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia saw no point in a sector-only ceasefire, reported the Kyiv Independent.

Trump made a similar claim in September. Neither side confirmed it, and both kept striking energy sites.

West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude benchmark, last settled at $91.66 a barrel. Brent, the global benchmark, closed at $104.42.

The war with Iran has already pushed fuel prices higher, as BeInCrypto tracked when oil passed $110 in April. Trump has since eased sanctions on Russian diesel exports and pressed Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries.

Bitcoin has already voted on the ceasefire. Oil, the market most exposed to it, votes next.

summary: Coinbase Asset Management President Anthony Bassili claimed its Bitcoin down payment for home loan products has “thousands of applications”.
content:
Grant Cardone said at the Bitcoin Treasuries Conference that discussing Bitcoin with Fannie Mae is "just too much."

Cardone claimed his firm is working on $600 million in agreements with $350 million in debt and anticipated lenders will regret not financing against Bitcoin.

In August, Fannie Mae-backed lenders started accepting Bitcoin for mortgage down payments through Coinbase and Better Home & Finance.

Cardone Capital founder Grant Cardone said he keeps Bitcoin (BTC) out of his Grant Cardone, the founder of Cardone Capital, said he keeps Bitcoin (BTC) out of loan conversations with Fannie Mae (FNMA), despite the fact that his firm connects the cryptocurrency with the apartment buildings it finances.

Cardone made the statements at the Bitcoin Treasuries Conference in New York during a panel discussion, published on Sunday.

Cardone said his firm is working on $600 million of deals that will carry about $350 million of debt. He said, "I never tell Fannie Mae I'm putting Bitcoin on it," and added that he never mentions Bitcoin to the lender "because it's just too much."

He predicted that lenders would come to regret it. Cardone stated that when Bitcoin reaches $400,000 or $500,000 in five years, "they're going to wish they gave me a loan on that Bitcoin, not on the real estate."

Cardone also targeted private mortgage insurance, which people pay if they put down less than 20%. He said it doesn't help homeowners. He said that whoever replaces it with a Bitcoin-based product would make a deal where "everybody's a winner."

Cardone said he has brought about 3,000 people into Bitcoin over the past 18 months by pitching real estate first. "I never talk about Bitcoin. I talk about the real estate," he said. Cardone has previously said he puts Bitcoin on the balance sheet of every building he buys.

title: Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana ETFs All in the Red for October
summary: Bitcoin ETFs have seen $386.3 million in net outflows through the first seven trading days of October, while Ethereum funds have now posted nine straight days of losses.
content:
"Uptober" isn't living up to its name for crypto ETFs.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $21.1 million on Friday, according to Decrypt 's ETF tracker. That's a modest bounce after back-to-back outflows of $484.9 million on Wednesday and $244.1 million on Thursday. Even so, the funds are down a net $386.3 million through the first seven trading days of October.

Bitcoin and other crypto asset ETFs allow investors to gain exposure to digital currencies without using crypto exchanges or wallets. These funds track the price of the asset and trade like stocks on a brokerage app. They've been very successful since their launch, and flows in and out of the funds have become a reliable measure of current market sentiment.

The month started strong , with $292.6 million in inflows across Oct. 1 and 2. A $118.8 million inflow on Oct. 6 couldn't offset the selling that followed, and Wednesday's exit was the funds' worst day since June .

That's a sharp reversal from September. After the Senate's failed cloture vote on the Clarity Act triggered heavy outflows in mid-September, Bitcoin ETFs reeled off a nine-session inflow streak worth roughly $3 billion . That run pushed 2026's year-to-date flows back into positive territory.

Ethereum ETFs have fared worse. The funds shed $56.1 million on Friday, extending their outflow streak to nine straight trading days.

They've lost $635 million so far in October and nearly $700 million over the full streak, with the heaviest single-day exit, $201.9 million, coming on Oct. 6. Cumulative net inflows since launch stand at $13.2 billion, and total net assets are $14.5 billion.

Solana ETFs are also in the red for October, though on a much smaller scale. The funds lost $3.8 million on Friday, their fifth straight day of outflows, bringing October's net total to a loss of $24.8 million. Their only inflow this month was $1.3 million on Oct. 2. Cumulative net inflows stand at $137.9 million.

For Bitcoin ETFs, cumulative net inflows since launch total $57.6 billion, and the funds hold $100.6 billion in total net assets, according to Decrypt 's tracker.

While 24/7 Wall St. has not independently verified Hashi's details, reports indicate it lets institutions raise cash against their Bitcoin without selling. The process involves locking Bitcoin in a multisignature vault on the Bitcoin main chain—a secure wallet that requires multiple approvals before anyone can move any coins. Currently, the data suggests that Sui is not poised to become the next Solana. With Solana's price 100 times higher and Sui down further from its all-time high, Sui holders face a significant uphill battle to make this comparison meaningful.

title: Ledger Wallet Spy Implant Scare Spreads To Europe As Crypto Losses Top $86M: Report
summary: Mark Karpelès confirmed the implant and said it reads the seed phrase off the device’s screen, the set of words that can unlock a wallet’s funds.
content:
A user said on Sunday that a Ledger device bought from an official European reseller had a spy implant, suggesting a scare that began in Asia may have spread.

Ledger confirmed that at least one affected device had an unauthorized implant. It traced the cases to Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, which has stopped all hardware wallet sales.

Trackers estimate losses at $72 million to more than $86 million across Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron. More than $10 million has been frozen so far.

A Ledger hardware wallet scare that began with Asian users losing funds has reportedly spread to Europe after a user said a device bought from an official European reseller contained the same spy implant.

According to Johannes, a well-known crypto twitter user who calls out bad actors, the device had been bought in a store a couple of weeks ago. "PSA the ledger incident isn't limited to Asia," he wrote on Sunday.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

He shared photos showing extra wires inside the device that a genuine Ledger hardware doesn't have. Johannes said the European device never sent funds to an attacker. He said it's unclear whether the implant failed or the attackers were waiting. He urged anyone who didn't buy directly from Ledger's online store to open the device and check it themselves.

Karpelès Lab CEO Mark Karpelès, who has been opening up tampered Ledger devices, confirmed the find. "Another spy implant confirmed," he said on X. He added that it looked like an earlier version of the implant he is studying, "meaning there were more iterations."

A hardware wallet is a small device that stores a user's crypto keys offline. When a user sets one up, the screen shows a seed phrase, a list of words that can restore the wallet. Anyone who has that phrase can take the funds.

The implant targets that step. It watches the screen to "take note and transmit the seed phrase you'll be setting up on your ledger," Karpelès wrote on Saturday. He said the implants have "evolved a lot in recent months," becoming harder to spot and easier to install. That means a device can look normal and still be compromised.

"The attacker may decide to steal your assets today, or in a year," Karpelès said. Anyone whose seed phrase was created on an implanted device should make a new one on a safe device and move their assets, he said.

Ledger had confirmed the problem in at least one case. "Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users' devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant," the company's support account wrote. The affected devices were sold through CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller.

Ledger said CryptoBilis has stopped selling all hardware wallet inventory until the investigation ends. The company said it has "no indication" that its own systems or services were compromised.

Ledger told users who bought from the reseller not to set up their devices. It said those who already have should move their assets to a new Ledger with a new seed phrase. Ledger has not said whether it is aware of any cases in Europe.

The scare surfaced Friday, when Ledger said it was looking into reports of lost funds from Southeast Asian users who bought from CryptoBilis. It asked the reseller to pause all sales and shipments.

On-chain trackers had already started counting losses. Security researcher tanuki42 put the total at more than $72 million, while analyst Specter traced more than $86 million from hundreds of victim wallets.

Blockchain analytics firm Arkham said over $80 million had reportedly been taken across Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Tron (TRX), adding that the cause was unconfirmed. Some of that money has been stopped. tanuki42 said that work with Tether (USDT) and law enforcement had frozen more than $10 million.

An all-time high represents the highest price a coin has ever reached. From that perspective, the rankings shift dramatically: Bitcoin is down 34.2%, Ethereum 49.5%, XRP 61.8%, and Solana 62.7%.

title: Bitcoin’s Price Prediction: Will Global M2 Point to $300,000?
summary: A chart circulating in crypto circles claims global money supply points to Bitcoin hitting $250,000 to $300,000, and prominent voices are taking it seriously. But the math behind it hides a flaw that lets anyone bend the prediction to fit whatever outcome they want.
content:
Bitcoin trades at $82,965, down 5.3% in 2026, yet a viral global M2 chart predicts prices between $250,000 and $300,000.

The chart's time-lag is chosen subjectively using past data, making it appear accurate in hindsight while offering no genuine predictive power.

Bill Barhydt cited a speaker's claim that Bitcoin must reach $300,000 within 24 months, which stands as the article's only concrete, testable prediction.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) is trading at $82,965 as of October 11, 2026, down 5.3% so far this year. Yet, a frequently shared global M2 Bitcoin chart circulating in crypto discussions posits a much higher potential price.

Bill Barhydt, CEO of the crypto firm Abra, recently referenced this chart on The Pomp Podcast . He stated, "If you look at the charts that everybody likes to show with global M2 versus Bitcoin, they're all saying Bitcoin should be around 250 to 300k-ish in that range," in an episode aired on October 8.

Many who share this chart may not fully understand what it measures or how it was constructed. So, can the amount of money in the world really indicate where Bitcoin's price is headed?

M2 measures how much money exists in an economy, including cash, checking accounts, and easily accessible savings like money market funds. The global M2 aggregates these figures across major economies, providing a rough estimate of the total money available worldwide.

The chart that often gets shared compares this global total with Bitcoin's price. Most versions of the chart adjust the money supply line forward by a certain number of weeks, based on the belief that newly created money takes time to flow through banks and markets before reaching riskier assets like cryptocurrencies.

------

Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.

That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›

------

This approach has its charm. Bitcoin has a capped supply, meaning if the money supply—dollars, euros, and yuan—keeps rising while Bitcoin's supply remains fixed, each coin should, theoretically, become more valuable. Simon Dixon echoed this view on The Pomp Podcast , commending Bitcoin for having "a monetary policy which you can rely upon with a fixed supply."

However, choosing the money supply line is subjective. Changing the number of weeks in the shift alters the chart's suggested "fair" price for Bitcoin, so the prediction can change whenever the creator adjusts the timeframe.

First, while some correlations may hold, they don't explain why this new money is flowing into Bitcoin rather than other assets like stocks or gold. For instance, U.S. M2, a significant portion of the global total, hit a new peak in August, yet Bitcoin is down 5.3% this year.

Jordi Visser offered one perspective on this potential connection on September 19's episode of The Pomp Podcast . He suggested Bitcoin often trades on liquidity, since its real-world use hasn't fully emerged yet. If true, the connection between money supply and Bitcoin's price might weaken as other factors take over.

Second, chart creators often select the forward shift after analyzing past data. They can test different time lags against historical prices and choose the one that aligns best, making the chart look accurate in hindsight while offering little insight into future movements.

Most critically, this overlay creates a price target that lacks a set timeline. This makes it unfalsifiable; no outcome can definitively prove it wrong since proponents can always argue that the price hasn't reached the predicted level yet.

To his credit, Barhydt didn't claim any specificity in his prediction. He said this price range "feels right to me based upon where the markets are going," indicating judgment rather than a precise calculation.

He also quoted a speaker from a treasury conference, without claiming the view as his own: "if bitcoin's not at 300k in 24 months, then my thesis on Bitcoin was completely wrong." This statement is testable because it provides a specific timeframe for evaluation.

However, those promoting the chart in this discussion have not published a track record, making it hard for readers to gauge how often their predictions align with reality. Treat any claims about its accuracy with skepticism unless the authors present both successful predictions and misses.

While money supply illustrates the liquidity around Bitcoin, it doesn't provide a clear price forecast. An increasing money supply can lift risky assets, but the global M2 chart lets its creator dictate the lag and set a price target without a deadline. It also fails to outline the path from $82,965 to $300,000, which would require new capital to flow into Bitcoin rather than stocks or gold within a specified timeframe.

The dated 24-month claim presents the clearest opportunity for evaluation. Readers can assess Bitcoin's price 24 months following Barhydt's October 8 episode. If it hasn't touched $300,000 by that time, the conference speaker has already said the thesis was wrong. Furthermore, if the chart's forward shift subtly changes after a mismatch occurs, it's likely being adjusted post-hoc to fit Bitcoin's price.

A halving is a scheduled reduction in the number of new bitcoins miners create and earn. About every four years, the reward for processing transactions is cut in half, so fewer new bitcoins enter circulation each day.

The theory behind the Bitcoin halving is rooted in supply and demand. With less new supply and steady demand, buyers will compete for the limited available coins, which should support the price. title: Who Really Owns Bitcoin? Wall Street vs. Ordinary People
summary: Who owns Bitcoin? Individuals hold two-thirds, while Strategy and Metaplanet find holding coins takes cash.
content:
Wall Street is pouring billions into Bitcoin, yet ordinary investors still hold most of the supply. Meanwhile, some of the biggest corporate buyers are spending millions to simply maintain their Bitcoin holdings.

Individuals own an estimated 13.9 million BTC, or 66% of the 21 million coins that will ever exist, according to Bitbo and River data compiled by Motley Fool.

That leaves institutional investors competing for Bitcoin that existing holders may be unwilling to sell.

As of October 9, Bitcoin ETFs held 1.48 million BTC, according to Bitbo. Companies controlled another 1.66 million, while governments held roughly 518,500.

Together, these groups accounted for about 17% of Bitcoin's maximum supply.

Meanwhile, around 1.6 million BTC are estimated to be lost. Another 968,000 sit in wallets linked to Bitcoin's anonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto.

However, ownership is gradually shifting. River data shows individuals sold a net 696,000 BTC in 2025. Businesses, investment funds, and governments purchased nearly one million coins.

If that trend continues, institutions may have to offer higher prices to persuade existing holders to sell.

Holding Bitcoin also comes with costs for companies financing their purchases.

Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, holds roughly 848,000 BTC. Yet its latest disclosure shows it drew $142.5 million from its dollar reserve for dividends and interest during the week ending October 4.

The company also spent $73.7 million buying back preferred shares between October 1 and 4. By comparison, it purchased just 334 BTC for $28.7 million.

Japan's Metaplanet took another approach. According to its October 5 disclosure, it sold 10,000 BTC and repurchased 11,000 during the third quarter to demonstrate liquidity.

The company now holds 44,000 BTC and has limited Bitcoin to 85%–90% of its assets.

With Bitcoin trading near $83,000, institutional demand remains significant. But Strategy's latest spending shows how maintaining a large Bitcoin treasury can compete with buying more coins.

title: China Launches National Blockchain As Part Of Wider Plan To Accelerate Expansion Of Digital Economy
summary: Despite having a traditionally conservative stance towards cryptocurrencies, the Chinese Communist Party is moving forward with the construction of a national blockchain network as part of a wider strategy to upgrade Chinese digital infrastructure.
content:
China has unveiled a plan to build a national blockchain network, but the Asian power's planned investment about the technology does not appear to equate to a slackening restrictions on private cryptocurrency trading, which remains banned in mainland China.

The measure was announced in a policy document entitled "Opinions of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council on Developing New Productive Forces." The document was made public by the official Chinese state news agency Xinhua on Friday.

The document made no mention of Bitcoin or other independent cryptocurrencies. Since 2021, Beijing has enacted a blanket ban on all cryptocurrency transactions. The ban extends to foreign cryptocurrency companies who attempt to provide services to people living in mainland China.

China does, however, operate its own sovereign digital currency, the digital yuan. Beijing has recently been encouraging its citizens to increase their use of the digital currency, having recently increased the number of banks authorized to operate digital yuan services from 22 to 30 in August.

China also already invests in blockchain, the technology which enables the existence of cryptocurrencies. China currently has a Blockchain-based Service Network (BSN), a state-backed platform which supports enterprise and government applications but prohibits cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin from operating on its rails.

It is possible, though unconfirmed, that the new system will build on BSN.

The document also called for a more comprehensive integration of the Chinese digital and real economies through the digitalization of the manufacturing industry, the construction of a "national integrated computing power network" and the implementation of the "Eastern Data, Western Computing" project, a mega-infrastructure venture designed to store data generated by China's economically productive and densely populated eastern regions in the less-developed, more sparsely-populated but resource-abundant west of China.

However, officials responsible for the digital transformation are also advised against "abandoning the real economy for the virtual economy, pursuing large-scale and comprehensive development, or creating bubbles."

The two government bodies in charge of implementing and regulating this expanded digitalization will be the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission and the National Development and Reform Commission. These two organizations will likely determine how the new blockchain network is integrated into wider Chinese digital infrastructure.

In response to the news, investor interest in China-linked blockchain project Conflux (CFX) has increased, with CFX steadily increasing since Saturday morning and surging to highs of above $0.07 on Sunday. At 8am EDT on Sunday, Conflux was hovering at $0.066, up more than 26% from Saturday's closing price.

CFX is widely seen as the only regulatory-compliant public blockchain in China because it works closely with state-backed corporations, does not sell unregulated tokens within Chinese borders and its founders have close professional and academic ties to the state-run Tsinghua University.

title: AI Uncovers XRP Ledger Bug: Is It a Threat or a Defense?
summary: An AI security system just flagged a flaw in the XRP Ledger that human reviewers missed for a decade, and the fix required breaking a decade-long protocol. Now developers across every major crypto network are asking whether AI accelerates their defenses or hands attackers a faster weapon.
content:
AI discovered an XRP Ledger flaw that could have minted 18.45 trillion XRP, a figure 184 times the total supply, threatening its $94 billion market value.

Engineers patched the bug within 3 days, with 80% of validators installing the fix before source code was released to prevent reverse-engineering.

Bitcoin's slow, public upgrade process leaves it far more exposed than XRP during the critical gap between a patch release and full node adoption.

A recent discovery by Veria Labs, a security firm, revealed a major flaw in the XRP Ledger that could have created an astounding 18.45 trillion XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) out of thin air. This amount is more than 184 times the original total supply of 100 billion XRP coins. Veria Labs warned that this bug posed a serious risk to XRP's entire market value, which stood at about $94 billion at the time of the report.

On September 22, 2026, researcher Cayden Liao, together with Veria AI, an artificial intelligence security system, identified this vulnerability. The issue stemmed from a single payment that could buy multiple trading offers at once. A counting error let sellers receive full payment while the buyer was charged almost nothing, creating XRP that never actually existed. Unfortunately, the safety check designed to detect such errors failed because of the same faulty counting code.

RippleX, Ripple's engineering division, said it found no evidence the bug was exploited. Nevertheless, AI's role in pinpointing the bug prompted engineers to revise their approach to releasing fixes for such vulnerabilities.

This revision affects not only XRP holders, with their digital asset trading around $1.39, but also investors in Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), priced at about $82,965, and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), trading at around $2,501. With that in mind, the question is: Is AI a significant threat to crypto, or is it becoming its best defense?

------

AI has identified a flaw that human reviewers missed for a decade, and the researcher who found it was paid to look. Cryptocurrency networks often run bug bounty programs that reward outside researchers for finding vulnerabilities before malicious actors can exploit them. In this case, the bounty system worked as intended, leading to a swift report of the flaw to those able to resolve it.

Engineers reproduced the bug the same day it was reported and patched it within three days. Over 80% of trusted validators, the computers that verify XRP Ledger transactions and ensure accurate records, implemented the patched software on its release day.

The XRP bug adds to a series of long-hidden security weaknesses in the crypto world that AI has helped uncover since July. Several of these discoveries have also involved Bitcoin. For instance, a flaw in the Coldcard wallet, which is a hardware device that secures Bitcoin keys offline, has been linked to the theft of at least 1,367 Bitcoin. Additionally, Core Lightning, software that accelerates Bitcoin transactions, advised operators to disconnect after similar vulnerabilities were discovered.

Although the Coldcard theft is unfortunate, these revelations bring previously concealed issues to light, allowing developers to address them. This suggests AI is bolstering defenses by clearing a backlog of vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.

RippleX engineer Mayukha Vadari shed light on the decision to bypass the XRP Ledger's usual release process for the patch. "Things have changed with AI. You can't just sneak in a critical bug patch in a regular public release process, because you're going to get caught and reverse-engineered right away," Vadari stated.

Attackers can compare new code with the old to pinpoint what has been fixed. Once a patch is public, anyone can do this analysis and see where to target unpatched systems. While this has always been true, machines now perform these comparisons much faster.

In response, XRP Ledger developers released binaries—ready-to-run program files—prior to sharing the underlying source code. This marked the first time a transaction-processing change was issued without passing through the amendment voting process that has governed such updates for over a decade. XRP had this speed advantage because developers could quickly mobilize a small group of trusted validators.

In contrast, Bitcoin lacks a similar system. Its rule changes go through public proposal processes that can take years to finalize, since no node operator can be forced to upgrade. This slow approach safeguards holders from a single group altering the rules, but it also makes the network less agile in fixing issues. Ethereum falls somewhere in between, needing many independent operators to install new software to implement upgrades.

The quick fix to the XRP bug has reignited the debate about transparency. Validators initially ran a program outsiders couldn't inspect, raising concerns about whether the network remains open-source, as many assume. The code was shared later, but holding it back temporarily denied attackers a clear path to unpatched systems.

Moreover, this issue extends to the cryptographic math that underpins every digital wallet. Justin Drake of the Ethereum Foundation has suggested that AI-driven mathematical advancements could pose a more immediate threat to the cryptography securing these networks than quantum computers. Michael Gutkin of Fireblocks countered that researchers have not yet demonstrated a breach of this cryptography. The ongoing debate centers on AI's implications for the development and security of crypto technologies.

For now, AI looks like a net defense. Since July, researchers have reported the flaws it surfaced, and the XRP Ledger fix reached validators before anyone exploited the bug.

The weak spot is the gap between a public patch and enough nodes installing it, and Bitcoin has no small group to upgrade overnight. If attackers exploit a major network inside that gap, AI could start to look like a threat.

title: Why Does Ethereum Fall Harder Than Bitcoin?
summary: Ethereum dropped more than three times harder than Bitcoin last week, yet it also gained far less during the month's rally. Something beyond simple volatility explains why ETH keeps taking the bigger hit without delivering the bigger reward.
content:
Ethereum dropped 7% while Bitcoin fell just 2%, then gained only 1% versus Bitcoin's 6% during the same month's rally.

Ethereum sits 50% below its all-time high and needs a 98% gain to recover, versus Bitcoin's required 52%.

Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) experienced a decline of 7.0% over the week ending on October 10, 2026, trading at $2,495. In contrast, Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell only 2.1% during the same period, trading at $82,801. Both cryptocurrencies fell, but when comparing Ethereum vs. Bitcoin, Ethereum's drop was significantly steeper.

Many Ethereum holders know the usual explanation: Ethereum tends to be more volatile, meaning it can fall harder and rise faster when the market shifts. However, data from the past month makes this explanation hard to defend. So, what really causes ETH to drop harder than Bitcoin?

Volatility refers to how much an asset's price swings over time. Traders often say an asset that consistently moves more than another, up or down, is more volatile. Beta is a related term that measures how much an asset tends to move compared to a benchmark. Therefore, a coin with a higher beta than Bitcoin often sees sharper price changes—up or down.

Many crypto enthusiasts hold on to the conventional belief that while volatility carries risks, it also offers rewards. The theory suggests that when Bitcoin rises, Ethereum should rise even more, compensating for deeper losses during downturns.

In this case, Ethereum's drop closely follows the theory. It fell 7.0%, while Bitcoin fell just 2.1%. However, if volatility drives these price movements, the expected rewards should be evident during upside periods.

While both cryptocurrencies gained over the last 30 days, Ethereum rose only 1.3% compared to Bitcoin's 6.4% increase. This time, as the market climbed, ETH lagged significantly behind BTC—contrary to expectations that it would outperform during rallies.

An asset that drops deeper yet gains less isn't offering the higher-volatility payoff. The traditional argument that higher risk leads to higher rewards doesn't hold here, as Ethereum isn't keeping pace with Bitcoin's gains.

Additionally, Ethereum trails Bitcoin even more when you compare each coin's price to its all-time high. Currently, Ethereum is trading 49.5% below its peak of $4,946, meaning it needs a 98.2% increase to return to that level. Bitcoin, on the other hand, is 34.3% below its peak of $126,080, so it only needs a 52.3% gain to recover.

This difference in recovery percentages makes Ethereum harder to recover. For example, if an asset loses half its value, it must double to get back to where it started. Therefore, any additional drop in Ethereum makes it harder to recover than Bitcoin.

The ETH/BTC ratio clearly shows how Ethereum is performing against Bitcoin. It indicates how much Bitcoin one Ethereum can buy, and as of October 10, this ratio stood at 0.03014. A declining ratio means Ethereum is losing its value relative to Bitcoin, and a rising ratio means it is improving.

Furthermore, recent fund flows might be contributing to Ethereum's struggles. Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) holding Ethereum—allowing investors to own ETH through standard brokerage accounts—currently have about $15.7 billion in net assets. Data from SoSoValue shows nine consecutive sessions of outflows, meaning more money has been withdrawn than added.

Such a steady outflow could put added pressure on Ethereum's price. However, there's no definitive proof that these outflows directly caused the price movements, as price and fund flows often move in tandem without one directly influencing the other. Additionally, a week or a month may not capture how these coins behaved in earlier recovery phases.

The evidence suggests that yes, Ethereum is taking larger hits without the expected higher gains. The analysis supports the view that Ethereum holders face bigger downturns without the corresponding price spikes that would justify the added risk. While the pattern is evident, the specifics of why this is happening remain unclear.

The ETH/BTC ratio will likely be a key indicator going forward. If it rises above 0.03014 during Bitcoin's next bullish phase and the current streak of ETF outflows reverses, it would show the catch-up behavior Ethereum's supporters promise. title: Most Investors Are Wrong About Who Owns the Most Bitcoin. That Misunderstanding Creates a Buying Opportunity.
summary: The people who hold Bitcoin have something that deep-pocketed buyers want.
content:
Ordinary investors, not crypto companies or institutional investors, own most of the world's Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC). Individuals hold about 14 million BTC, or approximately two-thirds of the 21 million BTC that will ever exist, according to River's Bitcoin adoption report for 2026. (River was founded in 2019 to "build the Bitcoin bank of the world.")

The distribution of the coin's supply has been on my mind for years now. But I've only understood very recently that other people's misconceptions about who holds the most of it represent a significant buying opportunity. Let's walk through the logic here.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The biggest single holder of Bitcoin is probably its pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, who disappeared in 2011 and whose identity remains unknown.

Many believe that the wallet addresses that are thought to constitute Satoshi's untouched stash hold 968,000 coins, or 4.6% of all that can exist. An investigation by Cointelegraph in September 2026 found that the estimates of the hoard's exact size range from just under 900,000 to about 1.2 million BTC. Those coins have never moved, and given Satoshi's potentially permanent absence, most people, including yours truly, assume that they never will, as to move them would cause widespread panic that they might be sold.

There are also an estimated 1.6 million coins that are permanently "lost," i.e., inaccessible to their owners. It is with some regret that I report to you that a small quantity of that lost sum was at one point under my control. Regardless, neither that pile nor Satoshi's are likely to re-enter circulation -- I'm certainly never going to find the wallet credentials I was using more than 10 years ago -- which has the effect of shrinking the pool of coins available to everyone else who might want to buy them.

Among the businesses that constitute the biggest potential buyers, Strategy has the most, with 848,000 BTC, or about 4% of the total; every other company combined holds about 3.9%.

As you can see, even exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as a group held just 7.1% of the supply despite being issued by major asset managers. And governments hold about 2.5% of the supply as of early October 2026 -- perhaps only a smidgen of what they could ultimately want to hold over the coming years.

So what does Bitcoin's ownership and distribution indicate?

In short, no single player can dictate its price by manipulating the supply, nor can a major holder manipulate the blockchain's policies, as owning coins does not confer any voting power over the underlying software or the direction that its developers choose to take.

The groups that are the most likely to want far more Bitcoin than they currently own, namely corporations, funds, and governments, today own only a minority of it. In 2025, individual holders sold a net 696,000 BTC while businesses bought 489,000, funds and ETFs 205,000, and governments 135,000, according to data from River. If that trend continues, River projects those three groups could own about 11.7 million BTC, or 56% of the supply cap, by 2036.

To own more, those groups need to buy it from the people who currently hold it by offering a price that the holders find attractive. Given that Bitcoin's supply is mined at a slower and slower rate after each of its halvings, over the long run it is thus quite likely that aspiring buyers will need to bid more and more to secure a portion of the supply. That's why I believe that buying it now will pay off later.

If you have the patience to wait for Bitcoin's slow-moving supply constriction to give way to higher prices, which can take years and is not guaranteed to happen, it's worth buying today and holding while the big accumulators compete for what's left. The big players can always choose to sell instead of buy, but in the long run, it's hard to envision what might make them dump Bitcoin and refuse to buy it again when its price is trending upward.
